deities: Karni Mata (14th-century warrior-saint, worshipped as an incarnation of Goddess Durga)
festivals: Karni Mata Fair - twice yearly during Navratri (Chaitra Shukla Ekam to Dashmi, March-April; and Ashwin Shukla Ekam to Dashmi, September-October) (verify exact dates before visiting)
Navratri - special celebrations, as Karni Mata is revered as an incarnation of Durga

history.dynasty: Rathore (royal house of Bikaner); present marble-and-silver structure completed under Maharaja Ganga Singh
history.period: Shrine origins circa 1530 AD, after Karni Mata's mahaprayana (151 years of life, died 1538); current form completed in the early 20th century (late Mughal style)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: The temple is NOT in Bikaner town - it stands at Deshnoke (Deshnok), about 30 km south of Bikaner on NH62/NH89 in Bikaner district, documented here with the corrected location. CSV DUPLICATE PAIR: seq 865 'Deshnoke Temple' is the same temple - see 865's file. The Karni Mata Temple is one of India's most famous shrines, known worldwide as the 'Temple of Rats': some 20,000-25,000 black rats, reverently called 'kabbas', live in and are worshipped in the temple - devotees believe they are the reincarnated devotees/kin of Karni Mata (the legend of her stepson Lakshman drowned in the Kapil Sarovar pond at Kolayat and Yama's boon reincarnating him and her followers as rats). White kabbas are considered manifestations of Karni Mata herself and are especially auspicious. Karni Mata (1387-1538) was the patron deity of the Rathore royal houses of Bikaner and Jodhpur; after her death the original domed inner sanctum was built circa 1530 and grew through devotees' additions; Maharaja Ganga Singh rebuilt it in its present marble form with solid-silver doors and carved facades in the early 20th century. Eating prasad nibbled by the rats is considered a high honour; if a rat is killed it must be replaced with one of solid silver (verify). Footwear must be removed; walking barefoot among the rats is required, and stepping on one is an offence - devotees tread carefully.

name: Karni Mata Temple
town: Deshnoke (CSV town 'Bikaner' is WRONG - the temple is ~30 km south of Bikaner city at Deshnoke, Bikaner district)
town_description: Deshnoke (also spelled Deshnok) is a small town in Bikaner district, Rajasthan, about 30 km south of Bikaner city on the highway toward Jodhpur, with its own railway station (Deshnoke, ~2 km from the temple). It exists essentially around the Karni Mata Temple and is one of Rajasthan's best-known pilgrimage destinations, drawing devotees and curious international tourists year-round.
tradition: Hinduism (Shakti; Karni Mata is the kuldevi/patron deity of the Charan community and the Rathore royal houses of Bikaner and Jodhpur)

travel.airport: Nal Airport, Bikaner - about 25-30 km (verify flight connectivity); Jodhpur Airport is about 220 km.
travel.railway: Deshnoke station - about 2 km; Bikaner Junction - about 30 km, well connected to Jaipur, Delhi and Jodhpur.
travel.road: On NH62/NH89, about 30-40 minutes by bus or taxi from Bikaner city; buses run every 15-20 minutes from Bikaner's bus stand (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather (15-25 C); early morning (5:00-7:00 AM) or evening for the most active kabbas and quieter darshan. Avoid April-June afternoons (up to 45 C).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00/4:30 AM to 10:00 PM daily (sources vary slightly - verify). Mangala aarti around 4:00-4:30 AM; sandhya aarti around 7:00 PM. Free entry. Dress modestly; remove shoes; no photography in the inner sanctum (verify on site). Offerings of milk/sweets for the kabbas are optional.
